description: Execute a list of tool calls in one request and one editor frame. Sub-calls run in order; each entry's result (unwrapped payload) and ok flag are reported in 'results'. Every operation the sub-calls record becomes ONE undo entry ('grouped_operations' reports how many were grouped). A failing sub-call does not stop the batch (error_count > 0 marks the whole response as an error, but earlier successes stay applied). batch cannot nest, and tools that need a rendered frame before answering (capture_screenshot in the windowed build) must be called on their own.

calls.description: Tool calls to execute in order

name: batch

description: List all scenes in the editor
name: list_scenes

description: List all nodes in a scene
name: get_scene_nodes

description: Inspect the Composer's composition passes and why each one drew or did not draw on its last render: name, enabled flag, whether it has a render-time is_enabled predicate, mesh layer ids, item filter bits, and last_result - one of never_rendered / disabled / is_enabled_false / no_scene_root / primitive_mode_disabled / no_mesh_layers / submitted, plus the scene view it last ran for and how many meshes its layers held. Use this when geometry is missing and a GPU frame capture shows NO draw calls and NO debug marker for the pass: a pass that returns early emits no marker at all, so the capture cannot tell a mis-gated pass from missing geometry. Note that 'submitted' only means the pass reached draw submission; its meshes may still have been rejected by the item filter. Also per pass: last_draw_list_entry_count, last_cpu_time_us / total_cpu_time_us / render_call_count (CPU wall time inside render(); reset with reset_composition_pass_stats), and a shadow_nodes array with the same timing for each Shadow_render_node.
name: get_composition_passes

description: Get detailed info for a node (transform, meshes, cameras, lights, joints, physics). The node is named by name, by path or by id. A Mesh prim reports world_aabb (world-space min/max) and skinned (a skinned mesh also its skin and joints, each joint with its inverse_bind_matrix, 16 floats column-major); for a skinned mesh the AABB is the POSED bounds derived from the joint transforms, unaffected by the mesh node's own transform (glTF requires skinning to ignore it). Also reports subtree_world_aabb: the merged world AABB of every mesh in the node's subtree (null when the subtree has no meshes) - use it for camera auto-fit on a whole object.

node_id.description: Node ID (preferred over node_name when both given)

node_name.description: Name of the node, or its path: slash-separated node names from the scene root node down, root's own name excluded (e.g. 'Parent/Child')

name: get_node_details

description: List all cameras in a scene
name: get_scene_cameras

description: List all lights in a scene, with cast_shadow and (when a view has rendered the scene) the light slot assignment from the last shadow pass under the active graphics preset per-light-type limits: shaded (got a light UBO slot), shadow_mapped, and shadow_index (2D shadow array layer, directional/spot) or point_shadow_index (shadow cube). Shadow casters beyond the type's *_shadow_light_count report shadow_mapped false and are shaded unshadowed; lights beyond *_shadow_light_count + *_unshadowed_light_count report shaded false.
name: get_scene_lights

description: List all materials in a scene's content library
name: get_scene_materials

description: Get detailed material properties
name: get_material_details

description: List all textures in a scene's content library
name: get_scene_textures

description: List all brushes in a scene's content library, each with its folder_path (slash-separated content-library folder hierarchy, '' = directly under the Brushes root) and its geometry_state (unprepared / queued / preparing / ready / failed). Brush geometry is prepared on demand: this query is a tier 2 consumer, so it ASKS the preparation queue for every listed brush and returns at once without waiting. vertex_count and facet_count are reported only for a brush that is already 'ready' and are null otherwise - a caller that needs the counts calls this again, or polls get_brush_geometry_states (which requests nothing), until the brushes it cares about are 'ready'.

scene_id.description: Scene id (from list_scenes); use to disambiguate two scenes that share a name. Takes precedence over scene_name.

name: get_scene_brushes

description: Report the geometry preparation state of a scene's palette brushes WITHOUT preparing any of them: per-state counts (unprepared / queued / preparing / ready / failed) plus the state of each named brush. Brush geometry is prepared on demand (tier 1 consumers prepare and wait, tier 2 consumers request and poll), so this is how a caller waits for a request_brush_geometry batch to finish.

brush_names.description: Names of the brushes to report on; omit or leave empty for every brush of the scene's content library

name: get_brush_geometry_states

description: Ask the brush preparation queue to build the geometry of a scene's palette brushes on worker threads and return at once (tier 2). The most recently requested brush is prepared first, and a brush already queued moves to the front. Returns the same per-state counts as get_brush_geometry_states, taken right after the requests were made; poll get_brush_geometry_states until nothing is queued or preparing.

brush_names.description: Names of the brushes to request; omit or leave empty to request every brush of the scene's content library

name: request_brush_geometry

description: List the node graphs a scene's content library holds - texture graphs (Graph_texture assets) and geometry graphs (Graph_mesh assets): each graph's name, its content-library path, its format token, its nodes (name, factory type, canvas x / y, parameters) and the links between them named by node and pin, plus the material slots fed from a texture graph (material_bindings) or the prims bound to a geometry graph (node_bindings). Names rather than ids, so a saved and reloaded scene compares directly.

scene_name.description: Name of the scene (default: every open scene)

name: get_scene_node_graphs

description: List viewport windows: window title, bound scene name, camera name, the pixel rectangle (x, y, width, height; top-left origin, the space of a capture_screenshot PNG) the 3D view occupies in the editor window, and the camera frame (camera_path, camera_world_from_camera as 16 column-major floats, camera_projection_type, camera_fov_y / fov_x in radians, camera_z_near / z_far). Use to verify which scene/camera each viewport shows, to crop a capture to the 3D view, or to reproduce the view in another renderer.
name: get_viewports

description: Headless pick probe: arm the pointer at viewport pixel (x, y) and run the same hover update a real pointer runs, reporting every hover slot (content/tool/brush/rendertarget/grid/bone) plus 'nearest' - the hit resolved by the same slot-ownership rule a viewport click uses (bone slot replaces content in bone selection mode; a bone hit reports the joint a click would select). The id-render readback is ASYNC: the first call at a position returns raytrace hits only; the armed position keeps the id pass rendering there, so call again after a few frames for the merged result that includes id-picked (e.g. skinned) meshes.

viewport.description: Viewport window title (see get_viewports); default: first viewport with a scene view

name: pick_at

description: Get this editor MCP server's identity: name, version, process id (pid), build timestamp (compile time of the server), and bound port. Use it to detect a STALE editor: if the pid/build does not match the editor you just launched, another editor.exe is holding the port and your calls are hitting the wrong process.
name: get_server_info

description: Show or hide an editor ImGui window by its title (e.g. "Inventory"). Windows do per-frame work only while visible, so headless verification uses this to open windows the default layout leaves closed. On an unknown title the error payload lists all window titles.

focus.description: With visible=true, also select the window's dock tab and bring it to the front (default false). A merely visible window can sit behind another tab of the same dock node, invisible in screenshots.

visible.description: true shows the window (default), false hides it

name: set_window_visibility

description: Frame pacing snapshot: display refresh period, pacer state (cadence N, margin, vsync grid phase), latest schedule decision, enforcement flag, simulated workload knob, and capture bounds (first/latest frame id). All times are seconds in the frame-record reference clock unless suffixed _ms.
name: get_frame_pacing_status

description: Per-frame samples from the Frame Pacing window's persistent capture (decision + frame time record joined). Times are absolute reference-clock seconds; 0 = not (yet) recorded. Use for offline analysis: achieved present deltas vs refresh period, grid residuals, latency, clamp waits.

first_frame_id.description: First frame id to return (default: latest - count + 1)

name: get_frame_pacing_frames

description: Set the frame pacer's application-commanded cadence floor N_min (FR1 set_min_vsyncs, behavior doc scenario 9). Raising above the current cadence downshifts immediately; lowering lets the normal upshift path (dwell + headroom) bring the cadence back down. Clamped to [1, 8]; applied at the next frame tick.

min_vsyncs.description: Minimum display refresh periods per frame (1 = uncapped, default 1)

name: set_frame_pacing_min_vsyncs

description: Set the Frame Pacing window's simulated CPU workload (U2 sliders, headless twin): each frame busy-waits a duration drawn uniformly from [min_ms, max_ms] inside the measured CPU slot, so the pacer sees it as real load. Clamped to [0, 60] ms, min <= max. 0/0 disables. Use for induced-load scenarios (P3.1) and W-response checks.

max_ms.description: Maximum extra CPU time per frame in milliseconds (default min_ms)

min_ms.description: Minimum extra CPU time per frame in milliseconds (default 0)

name: set_frame_pacing_workload

description: Configure the Frame Pacing capture: max_frames caps how many frames are recorded (recording stops at the cap; 0 = unbounded) bounding memory and the capture-size-dependent UI draw cost; clear=true drops the capture. Set the cap and clear together for a bounded 'record a run' capture, then read it back with get_frame_pacing_frames.

clear.description: Drop the current capture (default false); recording restarts immediately

max_frames.description: Capture size cap in frames (0 = unbounded); recording stops when the capture reaches it

name: set_frame_pacing_capture

description: Get currently selected items, plus active_item {name,type,id,scene_name,selected}: the one reference item of the selection, which can be an item that is no longer selected.
name: get_selection

description: Get undo/redo operation stacks
name: get_undo_redo_stack

description: Drop the undo and redo histories (queued operations are kept). Recorded operations are declared users / indirect pins of the assets they retain, so container unload can refuse until the history is cleared (R5.4).
name: clear_undo_history

description: Undo the most recently recorded operation(s) - Edit > Undo. 'performed' lists the descriptions of what was undone, newest first; it is shorter than 'requested' when the undo stack ran out. Operations that are only QUEUED have not been recorded yet and are not undone: settle first (get_async_status).
name: undo

description: Redo the most recently undone operation(s) - Edit > Redo. 'performed' lists the descriptions of what was redone, newest first; it is shorter than 'requested' when the redo stack ran out.
name: redo

description: Ask the editor to exit after the current frame, exactly like closing the window: unsaved changes are discarded. The response is sent before the shutdown starts; poll /health until it stops answering to know the process is gone. Used by ctest to stop the editor it launched for mcp_server_tests.
name: request_exit

description: Reset the editor to a fresh state, as a test harness does between test cases: clears the selection and the mesh component selection (mode back to object), empties the clipboard, drops the undo and redo stacks, the queued-but-unexecuted operations and the shader-debug stack, frees every thumbnail slot, restores every editor window to the visibility recorded at startup, and closes every open scene (unsaved changes are discarded). The scene closes complete on following frames; the call returns only once the scene list is empty, so no advance_time is needed afterwards. Persisted settings (editor_settings, graphics settings, window docking) are left as they are.
name: reset_editor_state

description: Get in-flight operation counts: pending/running async workers plus queued_operations (queued on the operation stack, not yet executed on the main thread), pending_scene_commits (worker-prepared scene changes waiting for the main thread's per-tick flush) and asset_loads (asset load tasks in flight, which change the scene when they publish). The scene is settled only when all five are 0. Also carries a lightmap_prepare sub-object: in_flight/regions_done/regions_total/cancel_requested plus last_result{committed, mesh_count, piece_count, tile_count, abort_reason} of the most recent lightmap_prepare_tiles.
name: get_async_status

description: Per-frame cost of Scene::update_node_transforms() summed over all scenes (plus the tool scene): last frame's pass/dirty/visited counts and lock/sort/propagate CPU milliseconds, a running per-frame average since launch or the last reset (frames, avg_*, peak_total_ms), and per-scene registered node bucket sizes (transform_update_nodes / no_transform_update_nodes). Pass reset=true to zero the running aggregate AFTER reading (the response still reports the pre-reset aggregate) - use it to bracket a measurement window.

reset.description: Zero the running aggregate after reading (default false)

name: get_transform_update_stats

description: Bake the static geometry under a node into that node's own mesh, one combined primitive per material, and REMOVE the merged nodes - the runtime fix for deep visual-only part hierarchies riding on physics bodies (each node under a moving body costs per-frame transform propagation + a draw). Merges only nodes whose sole attachment is a Mesh; nodes with rigid bodies or no_transform_update (nested sway spines, sensor carriers) are boundaries - kept, and with recurse=true (default) each becomes its own merge segment, so one call on a tree root flattens the whole rig segment by segment. Attachment-less chain/pose nodes whose whole subtree merged are pruned too (attachment-less LEAF nodes such as joint pivot anchors always survive). Kept nodes whose parent was removed are reparented to the segment root world-preserving. Undoable. Setup cost is significant (geometry merge + GPU mesh build per material per segment); merged parts lose individual pickability.

node_id.description: Root node id (takes precedence over node_name)

node_name.description: Root node name (alternative to node_id)

recurse.description: Also merge each discovered boundary segment (nested spines) as its own target (default true)

name: merge_static_subtree

description: Dump directional shadow frustum fit debug geometry per shadow node: F_shadow planes, their bounded face quads (the truncated view-frustum faces caster AABBs are tested against), and receiver frustum corners. Needs the Shadow Fit 'Collect Debug' setting enabled.
name: get_shadow_fit_debug

description: Shoot a ray through a scene's raytrace world and report the closest hit (mesh, node, primitive index, distance, position, normal). Uses the same mask defaults as the interactive viewport hover ray, so it verifies hover / ray picking behavior headlessly.

origin.description: Ray origin in world space [x, y, z]

name: raycast

description: Run a BATCH of geometry queries in one call; per-query results come back in order (a query error fills that entry's 'error' without failing the batch). Types: 'raycast' {origin, direction, max_distance?, mask?} = closest raytrace-world hit exactly like the raycast tool; 'closest_point' {point, node_id? / node_name?} = closest point on render-mesh SURFACE triangles in world space (distance, position, triangle normal, owning node; searched over the named node's mesh, or EVERY mesh in the scene when no node is given - name a node for big scenes). Built for placement scripts: probe the ACTUAL surface (e.g. a convex hull bulges past its authored points) instead of guessing offsets, many probes per request.

queries.description: Query objects: {type:'raycast', origin:[x,y,z], direction:[x,y,z], max_distance?, mask?} or {type:'closest_point', point:[x,y,z], node_id?, node_name?}

name: geometry_query

description: Select items by ID or by name / path (scene nodes, materials, etc.). Mirrors UI selection semantics: replaces the selection within the target scene only (other scenes' selections persist; ids=[] with no paths clears the target scene only) and makes the target scene the active scene. The last listed item becomes the active item unless 'active' names another one of them.

active.description: Item id (integer) or name / path (string) of one of the listed items, which becomes the active item instead of the last listed one

ids.description: Array of item IDs to select

paths.description: Array of item names or item paths to select, alongside or instead of ids (a path is slash-separated names from the scene root node, or a content-library folder path such as 'Materials/Metals/Copper')

scene_name.description: Name of the scene to search for items

name: select_items

description: Make one item the active item: the single reference item commands act on. The item does not have to be selected, and the selection is left unchanged.

id.description: Id of the item to make active

path.description: Name or item path of the item to make active, instead of id

scene_name.description: Name of the scene to search for the item

name: set_active_item

description: Delete nodes (whole SUBTREES) by id and/or name - the MCP counterpart of Edit > Delete, undoable through the same recursive-delete path, without touching the user's selection. lock_edit items and their subtrees survive (prefab instances always delete whole). Queued; settle before rebuilding into the freed names. Built for partial-rebuild iteration: delete one object's root group and rebuild only that object.

ids.description: Prim ids to delete (subtrees; any prim)

names.description: Prim names to delete (subtrees; any prim; exact match, all matches)

name: delete_nodes

description: Get the active scene: the scene that commands targeting scene-hosted items act on (the transform gizmo, mesh operations, delete/cut/duplicate). Follows selection changes and window focus; null when no scene is active.
name: get_active_scene

description: Make a scene the active scene, through the same activation path as focusing that scene's window in the UI (the gizmo rebinds to its selection, the window highlight moves, commands target it).

scene_name.description: Name of the scene to activate

name: set_active_scene

description: Apply a Transform tool edit (translation / rotation / scale / skew) to the currently selected node(s), through the same code path as the Transform window numeric entry. space=local applies values in parent space (requires exactly one selected node); space=global applies in world (anchor) space. end_edit=true (default) records an undo operation and refreshes the edit baselines; end_edit=false keeps the edit session open like an active drag, so repeated calls re-apply against the same initial state.

end_edit.description: Record an undo operation and refresh edit baselines (default true)

rotation_xyzw.description: Rotation quaternion [x, y, z, w] - must be a unit quaternion: a length off 1 by more than 1e-3 is refused, smaller rounding is normalized

name: transform_selection

description: Drag the currently selected node(s) through the Transform tool's drag path - the same one a gizmo mouse drag takes - spread over real editor frames: the drag starts like a gizmo press on a handle of that kind (the Move / Rotate / Scale tool is the active subtool, so a translate drag of one selected bone solves its IK chain when Bone IK is on, drawing the chain visualization), the target moves linearly from the start pose to the full delta over `frames` frames (one step per frame, the call returns when the last step is applied), and with release=true it ends like a gizmo release (one undoable operation). Give exactly one of translation, rotation_axis + rotation_angle_deg, or scale. A dynamic rigid body held by a live joint is pulled toward the target by a spring and moved by the physics simulation (the joints keep holding; release keeps its velocity); other dynamic bodies are held kinematic for the drag. With release=false the drag stays held after the last step (query the scene mid-drag); end it with action='release'. Keep frames small enough for the steps to finish inside the MCP request timeout (5 s); an expired call leaves the drag held.

action.description: 'drag' (default) starts a drag; 'move' retargets a held drag (release=false) at once - translation / rotation_angle_deg / scale are again the full delta from the drag start, of the same kind as the drag - and returns, so the scene can be read between moves; 'release' ends a held drag and records it

center.description: World center [x, y, z] of a rotate / scale drag (default: the gizmo anchor position)

frames.description: Frames over which the target moves (default 30)

release.description: End the drag after the last step (default true)

rotation_angle_deg.description: Rotation angle in degrees of a rotate drag

rotation_axis.description: World rotation axis [x, y, z] of a rotate drag (with rotation_angle_deg)

scale.description: Scale factor [x, y, z] of a scale drag

translation.description: World translation delta [x, y, z] of a translate drag

name: drag_selection

description: Drag a dynamic rigid body through the Physics tool's drag path - the same drag start, per-frame drag goal and release a right-mouse drag takes - spread over real editor frames. The grab point (default: the body's center of mass) is grabbed like a right-drag press; its goal moves linearly from the grab point to `target` (or grab point + `translation`) over `frames` frames (one step per frame; the call returns after the last step), and with release=true the drag ends like a button release (the body keeps its velocity). A body held by a live joint is pulled at its center of mass by a force-bounded spring toward a goal projected onto the positions the joint lets it reach, without the tool's damping / friction / gravity overrides; other bodies get the tool's rigid grab at the grab point with its overrides. With release=false the drag stays held after the last step (query the scene mid-drag); end it with action='release'. Keep frames small enough for the steps to finish inside the MCP request timeout (5 s); an expired call leaves the drag held.

action.description: 'drag' (default) starts a drag; 'release' ends a held drag (release=false)

frames.description: Frames over which the goal moves (default 30)

grab_point.description: World grab point [x, y, z] on the body (default: the body's center of mass)

node_id.description: Id of the Mesh node with the dynamic rigid body

node_name.description: Name of the Mesh node with the dynamic rigid body (when node_id is not given)

release.description: End the drag after the last step (default true)

target.description: World goal [x, y, z] of the grab point after the last step

translation.description: World translation [x, y, z] of the grab point's goal after the last step

name: physics_drag

description: Place an instance of a content-library brush in a scene. THE shape-reuse path: every placement of one brush shares its geometry and GPU buffers, so create a shape once (create_shape with add_brush) and place it N times instead of calling create_shape N times. Placement parameters are identical to create_shape's instance parameters. STRICT arguments: unrecognized keys are rejected, never silently ignored.

brush_id.description: Brush ID (from get_scene_brushes or create_shape add_brush; takes precedence over brush_name)

mass.description: Rigid body mass override for the instance; local inertia is rescaled to match (default: brush density x volume). Only meaningful with a physics motion_mode

material_id.description: Material by unique item id; reaches any scene's materials and the asset manager's loaded container materials (takes precedence over material_name)

motion_mode.description: Physics motion mode: static, kinematic, dynamic (default dynamic), or none = no rigid body at all (pure visual part, e.g. children of a physics-driven assembly)

name.description: Instance node name (default: brush name). Renames only the node; the mesh keeps the brush name so instances stay export-deduplicable

parent_node_id.description: Id of the prim to parent the instance under (any prim; default: scene root); the world position is preserved

parent_node_name.description: Name (must name exactly one prim) or path ('A/B', or '/A' for a child of the scene root) of the prim to parent the instance under; alternative to parent_node_id

pose_node.description: Insert an extra rigid (position + rotation, NO scale) pose node and hang the scaled instance under it as a leaf. Node scale scales the whole subtree, so use this for any scaled part that will carry children; the returned node_id is the pose node (the safe attach point, also for joint carriers - it keeps the rotated frame), mesh_node_id is the scaled instance

rotation_xyzw.description: World rotation quaternion [x, y, z, w] - avoids the select + transform_selection round trips - must be a unit quaternion: a length off 1 by more than 1e-3 is refused, smaller rounding is normalized

scale.description: Number = uniform brush bake scale (geometry, collision shape, volume and inertia all scale; use for physics parts; default 1.0). NOTE each distinct bake scale builds its own GPU primitive (shared by placements at that scale) - prefer few distinct scales, or the array form. Array [x, y, z] = node-space TRS scale composed into the transform (visual anisotropy, no new primitive; collision shapes do NOT follow node scale - pair with motion_mode 'none')

name: place_brush

description: Place MANY brush instances in one call (one request, one editor frame). Each placement takes the same parameters as place_brush (brush_id/brush_name, name, position, rotation_xyzw, scale, material_name/material_id, mass, motion_mode, pose_node), plus parent_index = index of an EARLIER placement in this same call to parent under it (its pose node when it used pose_node) - this is how chained structures (branch segments, nested parts) batch, since same-frame nodes are not findable by id. 'defaults' merges under every placement. On a mid-batch error the earlier placements stay applied and the error reports the failing index. STRICT arguments: every placement's keys are validated BEFORE any placement applies; unrecognized keys reject the whole call. Returns per-placement node ids in order.

defaults.description: Placement fields merged under every entry (e.g. brush_id, material_name, motion_mode)

placements.description: Placements in order; each = place_brush parameters + optional parent_index

name: place_brush_instances

description: Create a parametric shape using the erhe geometry generators, then place an instance in the scene and/or add the brush to the content library. Shape parameters: box (size [x,y,z], steps [x,y,z], power), uv_sphere (radius, slice_count, stack_count), cone (height, bottom_radius, top_radius, use_top, use_bottom, slice_count, stack_count), capsule (length, bottom_radius, top_radius, slice_count, stack_count; tapered when the radii differ, which requires length > |bottom_radius - top_radius|), torus (major_radius, minor_radius, major_steps, minor_steps), disc (outer_radius, inner_radius, slice_count, stack_count; annulus when inner_radius > 0; flat in the XY plane facing +/-Z), triangle (radius; flat XY), quad (edge; flat XY, double sided), rectangle (width, height, front_face, back_face; flat XY), regular_polyhedron (kind = tetrahedron / cube / octahedron / dodecahedron / icosahedron / cuboctahedron, radius; watertight - good CSG inputs), convex_hull (points = [[x,y,z], ...] in node-local space, >= 4 non-coplanar; watertight hull - THE way to get authored silhouettes like ship hulls; good CSG input). Flat shapes get a thin box collision shape - prefer motion_mode none for them. STRICT arguments: keys not in the placement set or the chosen shape's parameter set are REJECTED (e.g. 'radius' on a capsule - capsules take bottom_radius/top_radius), never silently ignored.

add_brush.description: Add the brush to the content library for later place_brush use (default false)

end_cap.description: sweep: cap the spine end (default true; ignored when taper collapses the tip)

inner_radius.description: disc: inner radius; > 0 makes an annulus/ring (default 0)

instance.description: Place an instance node in the scene (default true)

kind.description: regular_polyhedron: tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, icosahedron or cuboctahedron (default icosahedron)

mass.description: Rigid body mass override for the instance; local inertia is rescaled to match (default: brush density x volume). Only meaningful with a physics motion_mode

material_id.description: Material by unique item id; reaches any scene's materials and the asset manager's loaded container materials (takes precedence over material_name)

motion_mode.description: Physics motion mode for the instance: static, kinematic, dynamic (default dynamic), or none = no rigid body at all (pure visual part, e.g. children of a physics-driven assembly)

name.description: Brush / instance name (default: shape type)

parent_node_id.description: Id of the prim to parent the instance under (any prim; default: scene root); the world position is preserved

parent_node_name.description: Name (must name exactly one prim) or path ('A/B', or '/A' for a child of the scene root) of the prim to parent the instance under; alternative to parent_node_id

points.description: convex_hull: node-local points [[x,y,z], ...], at least 4 non-coplanar

position.description: World position [x, y, z] for the instance (default [0, 0, 0])

profile.description: sweep: closed CCW cross-section polyline [[x,y], ...] (>= 3 points; sharp corners stay sharp, author smooth arcs as dense points)

profile_end.description: sweep: optional morph-target cross-section (same point count), linearly blended along the spine

rotation_xyzw.description: World rotation quaternion [x, y, z, w] for the instance - avoids the select + transform_selection round trips - must be a unit quaternion: a length off 1 by more than 1e-3 is refused, smaller rounding is normalized

scale.description: Number = uniform brush bake scale (geometry, collision shape, volume and inertia all scale; use for physics parts; default 1.0). Array [x, y, z] = node-space TRS scale composed into the transform (visual anisotropy; collision shapes do NOT follow node scale - pair with motion_mode 'none'). For shape reuse prefer add_brush once + place_brush N times over N create_shape calls

shape.description: Shape type: box, uv_sphere, cone, capsule, torus, disc, triangle, quad, rectangle, regular_polyhedron, convex_hull or sweep

spine.description: sweep: bezier control points [[x,y,z], ...] (>= 2) the profile is swept along; frames are parallel-transported

stack_count.description: uv_sphere / cone: stack count; capsule: hemisphere stack count

start_cap.description: sweep: cap the spine start (default true)

steps.description: box: interior subdivision planes per axis [x, y, z]; 0 = vertices only at that axis' min/max corners (semantics changed 2026-08-10: was cell-pair steps, now subdivisions = cells - 1)

taper.description: sweep: (t, scale) keys scaling the cross-section along the spine; final scale ~0 collapses to a pointed tip

twist_deg.description: sweep: profile twist in degrees over the full spine (default 0)

name: create_shape

description: Set a node's transform directly by node id/name - no selection involved (no gizmo rebind, no kinematic hold on selected dynamic bodies). ABSOLUTE set semantics: each provided component (translation / rotation_xyzw / scale) replaces that component of the node's current transform in the requested space; omitted components are preserved. All provided components apply in ONE call (unlike transform_selection's one-component-per-call drag emulation). Applied immediately and recorded as an undoable operation; the node's rigid body is snapped (teleported, no impulse) to the new pose. Note: a node created in the same frame attaches on the next frame and is not yet findable - retry on 'Node not found'.

node_id.description: Node ID (takes precedence over node_name)

node_name.description: Node name (alternative to node_id)

rotation_xyzw.description: Rotation quaternion [x, y, z, w] - must be a unit quaternion: a length off 1 by more than 1e-3 is refused, smaller rounding is normalized

name: set_node_transform

description: Perform one complete inverse-kinematics drag gesture on a bone chain (undoable, one undo entry). The chain is discovered from the named effector node upward: bone ancestors are collected, stopping at (and including, as the fixed root) the first ik_lock bone. The chain is solved against the absolute world-space target - or against each position of path in turn, within the one gesture - and the solved rotations are written to the joints. The bone nodes' Ik.* properties supply DOF locks, rotation limits and the pole target; the governing pole is the one authored nearest the effector. Nothing here reads UI state (no selection, no gizmo, no Transform tool setting). The result lists the chain joints in root-to-effector order with their solved world positions, the lower chain's joints in effector-to-end-joint order under mid_chain_drag 'pin_chain_end' (lower_joints, empty without a lower chain), plus the governing pole's reference path and angle (null and 0 when the solve was unpoled), the effective effector_orientation, mid_chain_drag, solve_from, pole_alignment and pole_ease_distance, the pole weight of the last step (pole_weight: 1 under snap), and the number of solve steps.

effector_orientation.description: What the effector's own orientation does while the chain bends: 'keep_world' (default) keeps its drag-start world rotation, so only its position follows the chain; 'follow_last_segment' keeps its drag-start local rotation, so it turns with the joint that aims at it

mid_chain_drag.description: What happens to the bones below a dragged bone in the middle of a chain: 'rigid_children' (default) moves them rigidly with it; 'pin_chain_end' keeps the lower chain's end joint (the first bone below the effector, through single bone children, with no bone child or several) at its drag-start world position and rotation and solves the bones between toward it. With 'pin_chain_end' the effector is the lower chain's root, so effector_orientation does not apply to it

node_id.description: Effector node ID (the dragged end of the chain)

node_name.description: Effector node name (alternative to node_id)

path.description: World-space target positions [[x, y, z], ...] applied in order within one gesture (one undo entry); the last is the final target. Give exactly one of target and path

pole_alignment.description: How the bend comes onto the governing pole: 'snap' (default) swivels it fully onto the pole from the first step; 'ease_in' swivels it by the weight w = clamp(d / (pole_ease_distance * reach), 0, 1), d the distance from the effector's drag-start position to the target and reach the chain's total segment length

pole_ease_distance.description: Under pole_alignment 'ease_in': the drag distance at which the bend is fully on the pole, as a fraction of the chain's reach, in [0.05, 2] (default 0.5)

solve_from.description: Which pose each solve step starts from: 'drag_start' (default) solves every step from the drag-start pose, so the result depends only on the target; 'previous_step' solves each step from the pose the previous step left (the first from the drag-start pose), so a path's result depends on the way it went

target.description: World-space target position [x, y, z] for the effector. Give exactly one of target and path

name: ik_drag

description: Select bones relative to the named bones (doc/plans/rigging/skeleton_editing.md R10), as the Hierarchy context menu of a bone does: the selection within the scene is replaced by the bones mode selects, and the first of them becomes the active item (for 'chain', the first named bone). Acts on the named bones only, never on the current selection. When mode selects nothing the selection is left unchanged ('changed' false). Selection changes are not undoable.

bones.description: The bones to select from: bone node names (the first bone node of that name) or node ids. Every entry must name a bone

mode.description: 'parent': the bone parent of each bone; 'children': the immediate bone children; 'children_recursive': every bone below; 'chain': the chain each bone is on (up while the bone parent has exactly one bone child, down while the bone has exactly one bone child); 'mirror': the bone of the same skeleton (same topmost bone) whose name is the side-flipped name (arm.L <-> arm.R, arm_joint_L_1 <-> arm_joint_R_1, HandLeft <-> HandRight)

description: Flip Names (doc/plans/rigging/skeleton_editing.md R13): rename the named bones to their side-flipped names (arm.L -> arm.R, hand_l -> hand_r, HandLeft -> HandRight, a trailing index such as _1 or .001 kept) as ONE undoable operation, executed on the next editor frame. Two named sibling bones whose names flip into each other swap names. A bone whose name has no side, or whose flipped name a sibling outside the named bones already holds, is reported in 'skipped'. Acts on the named bones only, never on the current selection.

description: Clear Location / Rotation / Scale / All (doc/plans/rigging/skeleton_editing.md R14): set the chosen TRS channels of the named bones back to their rest transform (the Rig.rest_translation / rest_rotation / rest_scale properties, which default to the skin's bind pose) as ONE undoable operation, executed on the next editor frame. Channels locked by the lock_translation_* / lock_rotation_* / lock_scale_* flags (per axis, as the Transform tool enforces them) keep their values; bones with lock_edit are left alone and listed in 'sealed'. The result lists the bones that change ('changed'; unchanged bones are not written) and whether an operation was queued. Acts on the named bones only, never on the current selection.

bones.description: The bones to clear: bone node names (the first bone node of that name) or node ids. Every entry must name a bone

channels.description: 'all', or a non-empty array of 'location', 'rotation', 'scale' (the channels to clear)

name: clear_pose

description: Copy Pose (doc/plans/rigging/skeleton_editing.md R15): return the named bones' names and current local (parent-space) TRS as 'pose', an array of {name, translation [x, y, z], rotation_xyzw [x, y, z, w], scale [x, y, z]} in the order named - the argument paste_pose takes. Changes nothing, and does not touch the editor's pose buffer (the Hierarchy menu's Copy Pose).

bones.description: The bones to copy: bone node names (the first bone node of that name) or node ids. Every entry must name a bone

name: copy_pose

description: Paste Pose / Paste Pose Flipped (doc/plans/rigging/skeleton_editing.md R15): write a pose (copy_pose's 'pose' array) onto the skeleton the 'skeleton' bone is on, as ONE undoable operation executed on the next editor frame. mode 'normal' writes each entry's local TRS to the bone of the same name; 'flipped' writes it to the bone of the side-flipped name (arm_L_1 -> arm_R_1; a name without a side onto itself), mirrored across the X = 0 plane of the skeleton root's rest frame (the entry's change from its own bone's rest carried through the mirror of the parents' rest frames). Channel locks and lock_edit are respected as in clear_pose. Entries without a matching bone are listed in 'unmatched', not an error. Never reads the editor's pose buffer or the selection.

rotation_xyzw.description: Local rotation quaternion [x, y, z, w] - must be a unit quaternion: a length off 1 by more than 1e-3 is refused, smaller rounding is normalized

skeleton.description: Any bone of the target skeleton: a bone node name (the first bone node of that name) or node id

name: paste_pose

description: Create Bone (doc/plans/rigging/skeleton_editing.md R5): a new bone node (the persistent bone flag set) as the last child of 'parent' (any node; the scene root when absent), as ONE undoable operation executed on the next editor frame. Under a bone its head is the parent's tail (Rig.tail) and its tail is one scene unit along the parent's bone axis; under a non-bone the head is the parent's origin and the tail is +Y, one unit long. Local rotation identity; Rig.tail and the creation local TRS (Rig.rest_translation / rest_rotation / rest_scale) are recorded as local values; not connected. The new bone becomes the selection and the active item. Refused, with an error naming the skin, when the parent is a bone a skin lists (R9). Returns 'created' [{name, id, tail}].

name.description: Name of the new bone (default 'Bone'); made unique among the parent's children and the parent's skeleton as '<name>.001', ...

parent.description: Parent node: node name (the first node of that name) or node id. Default: the scene root

name: create_bone

description: Extrude (doc/plans/rigging/skeleton_editing.md R6): from each named bone a new CONNECTED child bone whose head is the bone's tail, with the same tail vector (same direction and length) and identity local rotation, rest values recorded, named '<base>.NNN' (the first free index in the skeleton). ONE undoable operation executed on the next editor frame; the new bones become the selection (the first active), so a repeated extrude grows a chain. Refused, with an error naming the skin, when any named bone is a joint a skin lists (R9). Acts on the named bones only, never on the selection. Returns 'created' [{name, id, tail}].

bones.description: The bones to extrude from: bone node names (the first bone node of that name) or node ids

name: extrude_bones

description: Subdivide (doc/plans/rigging/skeleton_editing.md R7): each named bone becomes 'count' connected bones along its head-to-tail segment: the bone keeps its name, head and rest, its tail becomes tail / count, and count - 1 new bones named '<base>.NNN' follow as a chain of children. The bone's other children re-parent to the last piece keeping their world transforms (and an unbound child bone's rest translation moves with them). ONE undoable operation executed on the next editor frame; the bone and its pieces become the selection. Refused, with an error naming the skin, when any named bone is a joint a skin lists (R9). Returns 'created' [{name, id, tail}] (the new pieces).

bones.description: The bones to subdivide: bone node names (the first bone node of that name) or node ids

count.description: Number of bones each named bone becomes (default 2)

name: subdivide_bones

description: Delete / Dissolve (doc/plans/rigging/skeleton_editing.md R8): removes the named bones as ONE undoable operation executed on the next editor frame. Their children re-parent to the removed bone's parent keeping their world transforms; an unbound child bone's rest becomes rest(removed) * rest(child). mode 'dissolve' additionally extends the parent bone's tail (Rig.tail) to the removed bone's tail when the removed bone was its only connected child, and the removed bone's connected children stay connected to it; every other connected child of a removed bone is disconnected. The selection is cleared. Refused, with an error naming the skin, when any named bone is a joint a skin lists (R9). Returns 'removed' [{name, id}].

bones.description: The bones to remove: bone node names (the first bone node of that name) or node ids

name: delete_bones

description: Symmetrize (doc/plans/rigging/skeleton_editing.md R13): for each named bone whose name has a side (arm.L, arm_joint_L_1, handLeft, ...) and that has no mirror counterpart, creates the mirror bone across the X = 0 plane of the skeleton frame (the frame of the skeleton root's parent node, in which the root's own transform sits), as ONE undoable operation executed on the next editor frame. Bones are mirrored parents first, so naming a whole side mirrors it whole. The mirror bone is named flip_side_name(name) and parented to the mirror bone created for its parent, else to its parent's counterpart, else to its parent; its local transform is the mirror of the bone's current world transform, its Rig.tail (x, y, z) -> (-x, y, z), its Rig.rest_* the mirrored rest, Rig.connected copied, and the bone's local Ik.* values copied mirrored (limit_min / limit_max: X range kept, Y and Z ranges negated and swapped; rest_rotation mirrored; pole_angle negated; pole_target mapped to the pole's mirror). Bones without a side or with a counterpart are skipped. The new bones become the selection. Refused, with an error naming the skin, when a named bone, or an existing bone a mirror would be created under, is a joint a skin lists (R9). Returns 'created' [{name, id, tail}] (empty and queued false when nothing needed mirroring).

bones.description: The bones to mirror: bone node names (the first bone node of that name) or node ids

name: symmetrize_bones

description: Recalculate Roll (doc/plans/rigging/skeleton_editing.md R16): turns each named bone about its head-to-tail axis (Rig.tail direction) so its local 'axis' points as close as possible to the world direction 'reference' (the axis and the reference projected onto the plane perpendicular to the bone axis coincide), as ONE undoable operation executed on the next editor frame. The head and the tail point stay put; children keep their world transforms (a connected child bone its head on the tail); the rest transform (Rig.rest_translation / rest_rotation) turns with the bone, so the pose relative to rest is unchanged, and a local Ik.rest_rotation turns with it. Bones whose axis or reference is parallel to the bone axis are skipped. Refused, with an error naming the skin, when any named bone is a joint a skin lists (R9). Returns 'changed' [{name, id}].

axis.description: The bone-local axis to aim: 'x' or 'z'

bones.description: The bones to roll: bone node names (the first bone node of that name) or node ids

reference.description: The world direction to aim at: 'x', 'y', 'z', '-x', '-y', '-z' or [x, y, z] (e.g. a view direction)

name: recalculate_bone_roll

description: Align to Active (doc/plans/rigging/skeleton_editing.md R16): gives each named bone (the 'active' bone itself excluded) the active bone's head-to-tail direction and roll, as ONE undoable operation executed on the next editor frame: the head stays, the bone's world rotation becomes the active bone's (times the shortest rotation between the two bones' local tail directions when they differ), so its tail keeps its length and points along the active bone's tail. A named bone's Rig.tail without a local value is recorded as one. Children keep their world transforms (a connected child bone its head on the moved tail and its world rotation); the rest transform turns with the bone, and a local Ik.rest_rotation with it. Refused, with an error naming the skin, when any named bone is a joint a skin lists (R9). Returns 'changed' [{name, id}].

active.description: The bone to align to: bone node name or node id

bones.description: The bones to align: bone node names (the first bone node of that name) or node ids

name: align_bones

description: Bind (rigid) (doc/plans/rigging/skeleton_editing.md R18): creates an erhe::scene::Skin for 'mesh' from 'bones', the editor-side counterpart of create_skin for smoke-testing an authored skeleton. The mesh's geometry is baked into world space and replaced by a new skinned mesh prim of the same name under the same parent (at world identity) with the mesh's first material; the skin '<mesh> skin' lists the bones in the given order (duplicates dropped). Inverse bind matrices are the inverses of the bones' REST world transforms (each bone's Rig.rest_* composed up the chain, the frame above the topmost bound bone at its current world transform), so the bind pose the skin implies is the bones' rest pose; every vertex is bound with weight 1 to the bone whose rest head-tail segment (Rig.tail) is nearest to it. ONE undoable operation executed on the next editor frame; its undo removes the skin and the new mesh and puts the mesh back. Afterwards the bones are joints of the skin, so the bound-skeleton refusals (R9) apply to them. Refused, with an error naming the reason, when the mesh already has a skin, has no primitives, a named node is not a bone or is in another scene, or a bone is already a joint of a skin. Returns node_name / node_id of the new mesh, skin_name / skin_id and 'joints' [{name, id, joint_index, vertex_count, inverse_bind_matrix (16 floats, column-major)}].

description: Build one rigidly skinned mesh from mesh prims already in the scene (undoable, executes on the next editor frame). Each entry of 'parts' names a mesh prim and the joint node that drives every vertex of that mesh: the part geometries are merged into a single Geometry with their world transforms baked in, and each part's vertices get joint_indices_0 = (joint, 0, 0, 0) and joint_weights_0 = (1, 0, 0, 0). The skin's joints are the distinct joint nodes in order of first appearance in 'parts'. The result is one new Mesh prim with one primitive, built with the skinned vertex format, carrying a Skin whose inverse bind matrices are the inverses of the joint world transforms at the time of the call; the part mesh prims are removed from the scene. Rigid weights only - the weight paint tool authors smooth weights. Refuses a part that carries no mesh, a part that is already skinned, an empty 'parts' array, and a joint in another scene.

description: Copy a content-library item from one scene's library to another's. Copies never alias: the copy is a fresh item owned by the target scene (brushes share their expensive payload by reference). Name collisions in the target get a ' (N)' suffix. description: Get a scene's per-scene state: ambient light color, physics enable, and the per-scene setting overrides (#239; null when every field uses the editor-global default, else the Scene_settings object: sky, grid, physics, shadow_frustum_fit, camera_controls, clear_color, post_processing).

description: List the variant sets a scene carries (doc/usd-compatibility-plan.md X4): per set the path of the prim carrying it, the set name, the variant block the set is declared inside (`enclosing_set_name` / `enclosing_variant_name`, both empty for a set the prim declares itself) and whether that block is the selected one (`enclosing_selected`, which is when the set's variants reach the scene at all), the selected variant, every variant with its material bindings, property opinions and the prims it adds (every variant's prims are in the scene; a switch flips their active property), and how many opinions the file's variants authored that are not carried and are not written back.
name: get_scene_variants

ambient_light.description: Ambient light color [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a]

merge.description: Deep-merge 'settings' over the current settings instead of replacing them (default false)

settings.description: Scene_settings object (same shape get_scene_settings returns): optional sky, grid, physics, shadow_frustum_fit, camera_controls, clear_color ([r,g,b,a]), post_processing (bool)

name: set_scene_settings

description: Select one variant of one variant set of a scene: the chosen variant's material bindings are assigned and the selection is recorded in the scene settings (Scene_settings.variant_selections), as one undoable operation. Switching a set applies what the block it selects declares, so a variant set declared inside that block comes on with its own selection and the sets of the block being left go off. Use get_scene_variants for the prim paths, set names, enclosing blocks and variant names.

enclosing_set_name.description: Name of the variant set whose block declares this set (as get_scene_variants reports it); empty, the default, names a set the prim declares itself

enclosing_variant_name.description: Name of the variant block this set is declared inside; empty, the default, names a set the prim declares itself

prim_path.description: Path of the prim carrying the variant set (as get_scene_variants reports it); empty names the scene's root prim, which is what carries a glTF asset's variant set

variant_name.description: Name of the variant to select

name: select_variant

description: Save a scene in its own source format, without a file dialog. A scene opened from a USD file (source_format 'usd' in list_scenes) writes a .usda layer carrying the scene graph, the content library's materials with their image files, and the scene-level editor state in customLayerData; every other scene writes a single erhe-authored glTF file carrying FULL editor state (render content plus the ERHE_* extensions: scene settings, physics, layouts, brushes, node graphs, collections/tags; ERHE_scene in extensionsUsed marks the file). The reply reports the format written. Without 'path' the scene saves back to its own source file when it was opened/loaded from one, else to res/editor/scenes/<scene name> with that format's extension. When the written file is a loaded prefab source, the prefab is reloaded so every instance in every scene reflects the edit (this subsumed the former save_prefab tool). This is the scene persistence path; export_gltf without editor_state is the plain interchange export.

path.description: Destination file path (default: the scene's source file, else res/editor/scenes/<scene name> with the scene format's extension). For a glTF scene, .glb is appended when the extension is neither .glb nor .gltf (.gltf selects the text form); for a USD scene, .usda is appended unless the path already carries a USD extension

set_as_source.description: Save As semantics: bind the scene (and its container record) to this path, so further saves write back to it. Default false: an explicit-path save is an export that leaves the scene's source binding untouched.

name: save_scene

description: Load a saved scene, without a file dialog: an erhe-authored glTF file (saved by save_scene) opens as a full scene with its saved editor state (fresh content library, browser + viewport windows; not undoable); a .usd / .usda / .usdc / .usdz file opens as a USD-backed scene, whose top-level prims are the scene's top-level nodes and which saves back as USDA; a foreign glTF opens as a new scene via the same path as open_scene. The load is queued and completes on a following frame; discover the scene via list_scenes.
name: load_scene

description: Open a FOREIGN glTF file as a new scene (same as the Asset Browser's Open context menu entry): creates a scene root + content library + browser window + a new viewport window showing the scene, and imports the file, all as a single undoable operation. Existing viewport windows are not modified. The open is queued and completes on a following frame; discover the scene via list_scenes (named after the file name). A .usd / .usda / .usdc / .usdz path is routed to the load_scene path instead, which opens it as a USD-backed scene. For an erhe-authored scene file, prefer load_scene, which also applies the saved editor state.
name: open_scene

description: Make a scene visible and framed in a viewport window, for headless capture. Binds the scene into a viewport (the one named in 'viewport', else the one already showing the scene, else an empty one, else a new window), looks through the scene's first authored camera when the file has one (untouched, as usdview does) or creates 'MCP frame camera' and places it so the union world AABB of the scene's meshes fills the view when it has none, and reports which in 'camera_source'. A scene opened from a file that authors no camera otherwise leaves its viewport bound to nothing and renders black. The viewport renders on a following frame: wait a few frames before capture_screenshot.

margin.description: Distance multiplier on the fitted camera distance (default 1.35)

scene_name.description: Name of the scene to frame

viewport.description: Viewport window title (see get_viewports); default: the viewport already showing the scene, else one is bound or opened

name: frame_scene

description: Close a scene: destroys its viewport and browser windows and unregisters it from the editor (same as the Scene row's Close context menu entry). The close is queued and completes on a following frame.

scene_name.description: Name of the scene to close

name: close_scene

description: Create a new, empty scene with its own camera, viewport and content library (same as the Create > Scene menu command). The new scene's content library is populated with the standard brushes shared from the default scene. The creation is queued and completes on a following frame; discover the new scene name ("Scene N") via list_scenes.
name: create_scene

description: Export a scene to a glTF file, without a file dialog. By default a plain interchange export; with editor_state=true the file additionally carries the editor-domain ERHE_* extensions (ERHE_scene settings, ERHE_brushes, ERHE_node_graphs, ERHE_collections) for full scene persistence, and baked graph-mesh products are excluded (rebuilt on load).

binary.description: Write binary .glb instead of text .gltf (default true)

editor_state.description: Include editor-domain ERHE_* extensions for full scene persistence (default false = plain interchange export)

name: export_gltf

description: Import a glTF file into an existing scene. The import is ASYNCHRONOUS: the response returns immediately, the file is read, parsed and made GPU-resident over the following frames, and the (undoable) import operation runs once that finishes. Poll get_async_status until asset_loads + queued_operations + pending_scene_commits are 0 before reading the result. Closing the destination scene while the import is in flight cancels it. With materials_as_references (R7 import-as-reference) the parsed materials are acquired from the source container through the asset manager and listed as reference entries instead of copied definitions.

materials_as_references.description: Acquire materials from the source container and list them as reference entries (default false: import-as-copy)

name: import_gltf

description: Import a USD file (.usd/.usda/.usdc/.usdz) into an existing scene as an undoable operation, through LightUSD Tydra: nodes and transforms, meshes, UsdPreviewSurface materials and their textures, cameras and lights. Values are read at the stage's default time code; UsdPhysics schemas are skipped. The file is read and converted while this call runs (unlike import_gltf, which is asynchronous) and the undoable operation is queued: poll get_async_status until queued_operations is 0 before reading the result. The reply reports node_count, mesh_count, material_count and texture_count. A load or conversion failure - and a build without USD support (ERHE_USD_LIBRARY=none) - answers with an error carrying the reason.

description: Scan a glTF file without loading it: per-category object names with their glTF 2.1 unique IDs (uid, when declared), extensions used, and scan errors

name: describe_usd_file

hold_name.description: Name of the debug hold that keeps the asset acquired

name.description: Asset name (identity fallback; must be unique within the container for file scope)

scope.description: Asset scope: builtin (manager-registered procedural item, e.g. palette brushes), scene_local (by-name lookup against the registry and open scenes), file (asset defined in a glTF container file)

uid.description: glTF 2.1 unique ID of the asset within the container (preferred identity; file scope)

name: acquire_asset

description: Release a named debug hold created by acquire_asset, dropping its usership of the held asset.

hold_name.description: Name of the debug hold to release

name: release_asset

description: Request unload of a file-scope asset's container. Refused while any asset of the container has users (the refusal names them) or the container is dirty (unsaved asset edits; pass 'discard': true to drop them). A successful unload verifies exclusivity: managed assets still alive afterwards are logged as undeclared users.

discard.description: Unload a dirty container anyway, dropping its unsaved asset edits

name.description: Asset name (identity fallback; must be unique within the container for file scope)

scope.description: Asset scope: builtin (manager-registered procedural item, e.g. palette brushes), scene_local (by-name lookup against the registry and open scenes), file (asset defined in a glTF container file)

uid.description: glTF 2.1 unique ID of the asset within the container (preferred identity; file scope)

name: unload_asset

description: Write a loaded asset container back to its file. A container open as a scene delegates to the scene save (clears the record's dirty flag); an authored material container (created by make_asset_external) is rewritten from its live materials (R7 asset-file save); a container parsed from an arbitrary glTF stays read-only (its file may hold unmanaged content) - discard-unload drops its edits instead.

path.description: Path of the loaded container to save

name: save_container

description: Load a glTF file as an asset container through the asset manager (one parse per container; a path open as a scene returns that scene's record). Returns the record id, per-type asset counts and identifiability errors.
name: load_asset_file

description: R7: acquire a material from a container file and list it in a scene's content library as a REFERENCE entry carrying its file-scope asset key (undoable attach). The scene save then writes an ERHE_asset_reference proxy instead of the material data. Accepted only when the defining container is path-bound (plan resolution 11).

name.description: Material name (identity fallback; must be unique in the container)

path.description: Container file path holding the material definition

uid.description: glTF 2.1 unique ID of the material (preferred identity)

name: reference_asset_into_scene

The file is written (export stamps the uid), the manager re-homes THE live object (meshes keep pointing at it), and the scene's library entry flips definition -> reference carrying the file key - the next scene save writes an R6 proxy. Not undoable.

material_id.description: Material by unique item id (takes precedence over material_name)

material_name.description: Material name in the scene's library

material_name.description: Shared material name in the scene's library

scene_name.description: Scene whose content library is searched (required unless clearing)

description: Adopt a manager-known brush / material into an Inventory grid slot exactly as a drag-drop would (Asset_reference::adopt; the slot becomes a declared user and its autosaved v4 key is the returned 'key'), or clear the slot's asset references with 'clear': true. Look up item ids via get_scene_materials / get_scene_brushes / query_asset_manager.

clear.description: Clear the slot's brush / material references instead of adopting

item_id.description: Item id of a manager-known brush or material (required unless clearing)

name: set_inventory_slot

description: Instantiate a glTF file as a prefab into a scene: the file is parsed once (cached app-wide) and inserted as a clone that stays a reference to the source file. Instances share GPU buffers; insertion is undoable. The FIRST instantiation of a file loads its template asynchronously and returns {instantiated:false, loading:true} with no node_id - poll get_async_status until asset_loads and queued_operations are 0, then find the node via get_scene_nodes. Once the template is cached (any later instantiation of the same file) the response is immediate and carries node_id.

position.description: World position [x, y, z] of the instance root (default origin)

name: instantiate_prefab

path.description: Source .gltf/.glb file path of a loaded prefab

name: reload_prefab

description: Set (or clear) one property of a loaded prefab TEMPLATE. Templates live outside every scene, so no item lookup reaches them; every instance of the template reads the edited value live through its reference layer (doc/property-system.md D33). Not undoable - a template is a projection of its source file.

item_path.description: Path of the template item below the template root ('' = the template root itself; 'Parent/Child' addresses deeper items)

prim_path.description: USD prim path the template was taken from; omit for a glTF template or a USD default prim

description: List the glTF prefabs currently loaded in the app-wide prefab library (source path, name, content counts)
name: get_prefabs

description: Capture the current rendered frame to a PNG file and return its path. Works in the headless build (the emulated swapchain is read back at once) and in the windowed build (the capture is armed and collected one frame later). With annotate_imgui_items the recorded ImGui items of the desktop host are drawn over the pixels as numbered magenta rectangles and reported as a number -> item table, so the screenshot names what can be clicked.

annotate_imgui_items.description: Draw a numbered rectangle over every recorded visible labelled item of the desktop ImGui host and report the number -> {window, label, rect} table (default false). Costs one extra frame, the one the items are recorded in.

annotate_window.description: With annotate_imgui_items: annotate only items of this window (by the name or display_name get_imgui_windows reports) or of its child regions

annotate_limit.description: With annotate_imgui_items: at most this many rectangles (default 60), so the numbers stay legible

Requires RenderDoc to be attached to the running app (on Quest: launch it from RenderDoc Meta Fork so the capture layer is injected) and an active headset view. An OpenXR app never presents a swapchain image, so RenderDoc cannot delimit frames on its own - this brackets the multiview render explicitly. The .rdc is written on the device and collected by the RenderDoc host; see doc/quest-renderdoc-capture.md.
name: request_renderdoc_capture

description: Push a shader debug view onto the viewport scene views: saves each affected view's current Shader Debug mode on a LIFO stack and sets the given mode, so pop_shader_debug can restore the user's own setting afterwards. Typical use: push texcoord debug, capture_screenshot, pop. Values follow erhe::scene_renderer::Shader_debug / the viewport's Shader Debug combo: 0 none, 1 vertex normal, 2 fragment normal, 4 tangent, 7 texcoord_0 (authored/interpolated UVs), 8 texcoord_1 (generated facet UVs), 9 base color texture, 10 vertex color RGB, 14 V.N, 24 metallic, 25 roughness, 32 texcoord_2 (lightmap UVs).

shader_debug.description: Shader debug mode to set (Shader_debug enum value, e.g. 7 = texcoord_0)

viewport.description: Viewport window title (see get_viewports) to affect only that view; default: all viewport scene views

name: push_shader_debug

description: Pop the most recent push_shader_debug entry and restore the saved per-view Shader Debug modes. Views closed since the push are skipped. Errors when the stack is empty.
name: pop_shader_debug

description: Enable/disable the GPU ray tracing renderer (issue #233: material-aware ray query compute shader with lights, traced shadows and glass, rendered into the texture shown in the Ray Trace window) and optionally show that window / adjust its settings. Returns supported/enabled state and the instance count gathered on the last traced frame. Requires a Vulkan device with ray query + position fetch support.

downscale.description: Output downscale factor, [1.0, 8.0]: 1 = one ray per viewport pixel, 2 = each traced pixel covers 2x2 viewport pixels; integer values display with nearest magnification, fractional with linear; omit to leave unchanged

enabled.description: Enable (true) or disable (false) the renderer; omit to leave unchanged

max_bounces.description: Max transmissive interactions along one branch, [0, 12]; omit to leave unchanged

max_rays.description: Per-pixel traced-ray budget for the Whitted branching loop, [1, 1024]; omit to leave unchanged

save_path.description: When set, read the ray traced output texture back and write it to this PNG path (sRGB-encoded for viewing)

show_window.description: Also show the Ray Trace window so the output is visible in screenshots (default false)

name: set_ray_trace

description: Enable/disable and tune dynamic diffuse global illumination (doc/ddgi-plan.md): a scene-wide probe volume is auto-fitted to the content bounding box, traced with ray queries and blended into octahedral irradiance / distance atlases that replace the flat ambient term for non-lightmapped draws. Returns the fitted grid (probe counts, spacing, origin), the derived ray/texel counts and the probe texture memory. Requires a device with ray query support.

enabled.description: Enable (true) or disable (false) DDGI; omit to leave unchanged

probe_spacing_m.description: Target world-space probe spacing in meters, [0.01, 64]; omit to leave unchanged

volume_padding_m.description: Padding added around the content bounding box before fitting, in meters; omit to leave unchanged

max_probes.description: Upper bound on total probe count, [8, 262144]; the spacing is grown until the grid fits; omit to leave unchanged

rays_per_probe.description: Rays traced per probe per update, [8, 1024], rounded up to the trace workgroup size; omit to leave unchanged

hysteresis.description: Temporal blend weight kept from the previous probe state, [0.0, 0.999]; omit to leave unchanged

intensity.description: Multiplier applied to sampled irradiance before it replaces the ambient term; omit to leave unchanged

show_window.description: Also show the DDGI window so the probe atlases are visible in screenshots (default false)

debug_draw_probes.description: Draw a wire sphere at every probe (green active, red classified-inactive) plus the volume box; omit to leave unchanged

description: Activate dynamic rigid bodies (bodies enter the world deactivated). Scoped since 2026-08-09: node_ids wakes exactly those nodes' bodies, node_id/node_name wakes the SUBTREE under that node (union when combined); no filter wakes the whole scene. Scope iterative re-settles (--only rebuilds) so already-settled structures elsewhere stay asleep.

node_id.description: Wake every dynamic body in this node's subtree (takes precedence over node_name)

node_name.description: Subtree filter by node name (alternative to node_id)

name: wake_physics_bodies

description: Apply an external force / torque / impulse to a dynamic rigid body (world space, activates the body). Forces and torques accumulate for the next fixed step only (re-apply for a sustained push); impulses change velocity immediately. 'point' (world position) makes force / impulse act at that point instead of the center of mass.

impulse.description: Impulse [x, y, z] in newton seconds

node_id.description: Node ID (preferred over node_name when both given)

node_name.description: Node name (used when node_id is absent)

point.description: World position where force / impulse is applied (default: center of mass)

torque.description: Torque [x, y, z] in newton meters

name: apply_physics_force

description: List the shared physics content-library items (physics materials, collision filters, joint settings) with full properties
name: get_physics_items

description: Attach a new rigid body (Node_physics) to a scene node (undoable). One rigid body per node.

angular_velocity.description: Initial angular velocity [x, y, z] (world space, applied at body creation)

center_of_mass.description: Center of mass offset [x, y, z]

filter_name.description: Collision filter name from the content library (empty string clears)

half_extents.description: Box / cylinder half extents [x, y, z] (default [0.5, 0.5, 0.5])

is_trigger.description: Create as a sensor / trigger volume

linear_velocity.description: Initial linear velocity [x, y, z] (world space, applied at body creation)

mass.description: Mass; 0 = spec infinite-mass convention; omitted = derived from the shape

material_name.description: Physics material name from the content library (empty string clears)

motion_mode.description: Motion mode (default dynamic; kinematic = kinematic physical)

node_id.description: Node ID (preferred over node_name when both given)

node_name.description: Node name (used when node_id is absent)

shape.description: Collision shape; auto (default) = convex hull from the node's mesh, unit box when the node has no mesh. mesh shapes are static/kinematic only.

wake.description: Wake the (dynamic) body as soon as it enters the world instead of starting asleep; replaces a follow-up wake_physics_bodies pass

angular_velocity.description: Initial angular velocity [x, y, z] (world space, applied at body creation)

description: CSG boolean between mesh nodes (queued, undoable as ONE operation): target <operation> tool(s), composed in WORLD space. The result geometry REPLACES the target node's mesh primitives in place - the target keeps its node id, name, transform, children, material and physics attachment (collision shape is rebuilt as a convex hull of the result). The tool nodes are then REMOVED from the scene (their children, if any, reparent to the tool's parent - pass leaf mesh nodes as tools). Multiple tools (tool_node_ids) merge into ONE tool solid and apply in a single pass - STRONGLY preferred over sequential calls (each pass re-triangulates the whole target, and stacked passes leave sliver-triangle shading artifacts). Inputs should be closed watertight manifolds (capped cones etc.); an empty result leaves the scene unchanged and logs a message. Note: on a pooled brush instance the edited target silently goes private (same rule as the other geometry ops). Executes on the target's scene; poll get_async_status before reading the result.

The source mesh needs interior vertices to bend (a 4-vertex quad cannot billow - use a box with steps, e.g. size [w,h,0.02] steps [8,8,1]). Topology is unchanged.
