description: Prepare world-space lightmap tiles: make every lightmapped mesh/primitive instance unique, bake its node transform into the vertices (world space), clip the geometry against the spatial kd tile planes (clip vertices are binary exact across the two tiles sharing a plane) and re-unwrap each piece's channel-2 UVs at world-space density. Pieces become Mesh_primitives of new meshes under the identity 'Lightmap Pieces' group node; originals stay in the scene for lightmap_revert_tiles / re-prepare. Self-contained: the spatial grid split is computed from geometry alone and the per-tile density comes from the grid (tile_texture_size / cell size). On commit the display atlas clears to white and a single bake iteration runs automatically, then pauses (with the pause autosave). ASYNC by default: returns {queued:true} immediately and the heavy phase runs in the background while the old partition stays live; poll get_async_status until pending + running + queued_operations == 0, then read its lightmap_prepare.last_result (a mid-flight primitive swap aborts the commit and keeps the old partition; cancel with lightmap_prepare_cancel). Refuses while async mesh operations or another prepare are in flight. Toggle rendering between originals and pieces with lightmap_set_render.

resident_tile_budget.description: Resident tile budget; default = Lightmap settings value

scene_name.description: Name of the scene to partition

tile_texture_size.description: Texel side of one spatial tile (pow2 256..8192); default = Lightmap settings value

wait.description: Block until the partition commits and return the full per-piece manifest (small scenes only: the MCP HTTP response is dropped after 5 s while the work still completes). Default false

name: lightmap_prepare_tiles

description: Request cancellation of an in-flight lightmap_prepare_tiles: remaining regions are skipped, the results are discarded and the OLD partition is kept. Does not wait - poll get_async_status until pending drains. Idempotent.
name: lightmap_prepare_cancel

description: Revert the world-space lightmap partition: destroy the 'Lightmap Pieces' group and restore original mesh visibility. Originals were never modified, so this is always safe.
name: lightmap_revert_tiles

description: Toggle 'render with lightmaps' for the world-space partition: ON renders the piece meshes (all lightmapped geometry regardless of tile residency; non-resident tiles fall back to white) and hides the originals, OFF restores the originals. Call without 'enabled' to query.

enabled.description: Render pieces (true) or originals (false); omit to query

name: lightmap_set_render

description: List the lightmap quadtree grid tiles of the current layout: per tile its grid key {level, ix, iz} (cells anchored at multiples of the cell size from the world origin; level 0 = lightmap.cell_size_m, +1 halves the cell / doubles density, -1 doubles the cell), cell size, nominal texels/m, down-only density flex, content/residency flags and cell bounds - plus the scene's stored overrides.
name: lightmap_get_tiles

description: Subdivide one lightmap grid leaf tile {level, ix, iz} into 4 half-size cells (2x nominal texel density). The override persists in the scene (Scene_settings::lightmap_tile_overrides); with a live partition an async re-prepare is launched (poll get_async_status), otherwise the layout updates on the next bake tick. Get keys from lightmap_get_tiles.

ix.description: Cell X index at that level

iz.description: Cell Z index at that level

level.description: Quadtree level of the tile to subdivide (from lightmap_get_tiles)

name: lightmap_subdivide_tile

description: Merge one lightmap grid leaf tile {level, ix, iz} AND its 3 siblings into their parent cell (half nominal texel density). All 4 siblings must currently be leaves. The override persists in the scene; with a live partition an async re-prepare is launched (poll get_async_status). Get keys from lightmap_get_tiles.

ix.description: Cell X index at that level

iz.description: Cell Z index at that level

level.description: Quadtree level of one of the 4 sibling tiles to merge (from lightmap_get_tiles)

name: lightmap_merge_tile

description: Toggle the interactive progressive lightmap bake (per-frame budgeted gather with accumulation; direct light + indirect bounces; scene edits restart convergence). enabled:false PAUSES - accumulation and sweep counts are kept, the viewport keeps showing the published bake, the resident tiles autosave to <scene>.lightmap/, and enabled:true continues where it paused (reset is the explicit restart). single_iteration advances the bake until every active tile reaches the current minimum sweep count + 1, then pauses (autosaving too; repeated calls advance all tiles in lockstep). Reports bake status (sweeps completed, cursor row) and can write a tone-mapped debug PNG of the published atlas. Call without 'enabled' to just query status.

debug_png.description: Optional path for a tone-mapped PNG of the published atlas

enabled.description: Turn interactive baking on/off (off = pause; accumulation kept); omit to leave unchanged

single_iteration.description: Bake one more full sweep of every active tile, then pause

name: lightmap_set_baking

description: Set the orientation reference frame (transform space) of the transform tool: global/world (world axes), local (selection's own orientation), reference (a chosen reference node's orientation), or selection (a frame derived from the active mesh-component selection). For reference mode, give reference_node_id or reference_node_name (searched across scenes, or within scene_name when given) - this is how you set the reference. edge_normal_blend tunes the selection-mode frame. Read the current state back with get_transform_state.

edge_normal_blend.description: Selection mode: [0,1] blend between the two faces sharing a selected edge

mode.description: Transform space / reference mode ('world' is an alias for 'global')

scene_name.description: Scene to resolve reference_node in (optional; otherwise all scenes are searched)

name: set_transform_reference_mode

description: Read the transform tool's current state: reference frame / transform space (reference_mode: global/local/reference/selection), the chosen reference_node (for reference mode), edge_normal_blend (selection mode), the mesh transform_mode (move/extrude/...), whether a mesh-component selection is driving the gizmo (component_mode), the selected node count, and the resolved world-space anchor_frame (origin + orientation the gizmo and local-space numeric edits operate in). Complements set_transform_reference_mode / set_transform_mode.
name: get_transform_state

description: Set what the transform tool does to a mesh-component (vertex/edge/face) selection when the gizmo is dragged: move (translate/rotate/scale in place), extrude (duplicate the selection boundary, bridge it with new faces, then move along the gizmo delta), extrude_group_normal (same topology, but each disjoint selection subset slides along its own average normal by an amount derived from the drag), or extrude_vertex_normal (same topology, but each vertex slides along its own normal). Persisted in editor settings; applies to subsequent component edits.
name: set_transform_mode

description: Show or hide the transform gizmo handle sets (translate arrows, rotate rings, scale handles) and choose the scale gizmo style (basic axis/plane/uniform handles, or bounding_box face cones). This is the scriptable equivalent of activating the Move/Rotate/Scale tool from the hotbar or toggling the viewport-toolbar gizmo buttons, which are otherwise mouse-only. Omitted flags keep their current value; returns the resulting state.
name: set_gizmo_visibility

description: List the geometry node graph the Geometry Graph window currently targets: nodes with ids, type labels, input/output pins (slot, key, name, connection count), per-output payload summaries (geometry vertex/facet counts, point/instance counts, scalar values) and all links. 'selected' is true when the window has a target (a Graph Mesh asset). Waits for any background graph evaluation to finish, so the payloads reflect all previously issued mutations.
name: get_geometry_graph

description: Point the Geometry Graph window (and the geometry_graph_* tools) at a Graph Mesh asset by name, or clear the target with an empty/omitted name. This replaces the old 'select the asset to edit it' behaviour - the window no longer follows the global selection (issue #252).

graph_mesh.description: Name of the Graph Mesh asset to target; empty or omitted clears the target

name: set_geometry_graph_target

description: Add a node to the geometry node graph. Returns the new node's id and pin layout. Structural edits (add/remove/connect/disconnect) schedule the automatic DAG canvas layout, applied when the window next draws.
name: geometry_graph_add_node

description: Connect an output pin of one geometry graph node to an input pin of another (pins are addressed by node id + pin slot index; pin keys must match). Undoable; the graph re-evaluates in the background (get_geometry_graph waits for completion, get_async_status reports progress).

sink_node_id.description: Id of the node receiving the input

sink_slot.description: Input pin slot index on the sink node (default 0)

source_node_id.description: Id of the node providing the output

source_slot.description: Output pin slot index on the source node (default 0)

name: geometry_graph_connect

description: Disconnect a geometry graph link (addressed like geometry_graph_connect). Undoable.

sink_node_id.description: Id of the node receiving the input

sink_slot.description: Input pin slot index on the sink node (default 0)

source_node_id.description: Id of the node providing the output

source_slot.description: Output pin slot index on the source node (default 0)

name: geometry_graph_disconnect

description: Remove a geometry graph node (its links are removed too). Undoable.

node_id.description: Id of the node to remove

name: geometry_graph_remove_node

description: Set parameters of a geometry graph node. Takes the same JSON object shape as the graph file's per-node 'parameters' (see get_geometry_graph); partial updates are allowed - omitted keys keep their current values. Undoable; the graph re-evaluates in the background (get_geometry_graph waits for completion, get_async_status reports progress).

node_id.description: Id of the node

name: geometry_graph_set_parameter

description: Set or clear a geometry graph node's display / ghost designation (Houdini display / template flags). The display node's geometry replaces the output node's wired input in the scene bake (render mesh AND physics); the ghost node's geometry additionally shows as a dim edge-lines-only mesh (no shadow, not pickable). One node each per graph: setting a flag moves it from any previous holder; false clears the flag only when this node holds it. Undoable; the graph re-bakes in the background (get_geometry_graph waits and reports display_node_id / ghost_node_id).

display.description: true: make this the display node; false: clear the display flag if this node holds it

ghost.description: true: make this the ghost node; false: clear the ghost flag if this node holds it

node_id.description: Id of the node to (un)designate

name: geometry_graph_set_display_flags

description: Enable/disable per-node mesh preview thumbnails on the geometry graph canvas (the 'Show node previews' checkbox; editor-global persistent setting, ON by default). Enabling forces a full background re-evaluation of every graph so every node gets a preview; previews render a few nodes per frame after evaluation completes.

enabled.description: true (default) to show previews, false to hide

name: geometry_graph_set_node_previews

description: Set (or clear) the canvas routing mid points of a geometry graph link, optionally with explicit pen-tool tangent handles per point. Mid points are canvas-space control points the link's wire is routed through (on-canvas gestures: double-click a link to add one, double-click a handle to remove it, drag a handle to move it; on a SELECTED link each point shows tangent dots - dragging one captures the computed tangents and switches the point to mirrored, Alt-drag breaks it to free, double-click on a dot resets to auto). The link is identified by its endpoint pins (see get_geometry_graph 'links'); the whole mid point list is replaced. Omitted / empty mid_points clears the routing (plain direct wire). Canvas-only state: not undoable, not saved to the scene, but carried by canvas copy / paste (unlike node POSITIONS, which are stored on the nodes, shared by every editor window and saved with the graph). get_geometry_graph reports each link's current 'mid_points' in the same dual entry form.

mid_points.description: Control points ordered from source to sink; empty / omitted clears. Each entry is a canvas-space [x, y] pair (Auto tangents) or an object {pos:[x,y], mode:1|2|3, in:[x,y], out:[x,y]} with explicit pen-tool tangent offsets (mode 1 mirrored, 2 aligned, 3 free)

sink_slot.description: Input pin slot on the sink node (default 0)

source_slot.description: Output pin slot on the source node (default 0)

name: geometry_graph_set_link_mid_points

description: Set a geometry graph link's per-link curve shape (Kochanek-Bartels tension / continuity / bias, each clamped to [-1, 1]; all 0 = the default routing). Tension scales tangent lengths (+1 makes the link a polyline, negative swings wider); continuity and bias reshape the tangents at the link's routing mid points (no visible effect on a link without mid points). Canvas-only state (like mid points): not undoable, not saved to the scene, but carried by canvas copy / paste. Also editable in the Node Properties window when the link is selected on the canvas. get_geometry_graph reports each link's non-default params as 'curve' [tension, continuity, bias].

bias.description: Tangent lean at mid points, -1..1 (default 0; +1 leans towards the incoming chord)

continuity.description: Tangent split at mid points, -1..1 (default 0; +/-1 = corners)

sink_slot.description: Input pin slot on the sink node (default 0)

source_slot.description: Output pin slot on the source node (default 0)

tension.description: Tangent length scale, -1..1 (default 0; +1 = polyline, negative = wider swing)

name: geometry_graph_set_link_curve

description: Show the Geometry Graph window and set its node-editor zoom (view scale) immediately, centered on the graph content. zoom > 1 zooms in (content drawn larger), zoom < 1 zooms out. Deterministic (no animation / no mouse input) - intended for headless zoom-quality verification (capture_screenshot on the next frame). Requires the window to have a target Graph Mesh (create_graph_mesh / set_geometry_graph_target) for it to render nodes.

zoom.description: View scale (> 0). 1.0 = native, 2.0 = 2x zoom in, 0.5 = 2x zoom out.

name: geometry_graph_set_view

description: Add one node of every texture graph node type to the selected Graph Texture, laid out in a grid. Same action as the canvas background context menu's "Add all"; adds as a single compound undo entry. Intended for visual verification - it puts the whole node library on the canvas at once, where a node that fails to compose, renders black or mis-lays-out its widgets is obvious. The grid layout applies once the canvas has measured every node, so render a few frames (or texture_graph_set_view + capture_screenshot) before judging positions.
name: texture_graph_add_all

description: Show the Texture Graph window and set its node-editor zoom (view scale) immediately, centered on the graph content. zoom > 1 zooms in (content drawn larger), zoom < 1 zooms out. Deterministic (no animation / no mouse input) - intended for headless zoom-quality verification (capture_screenshot on the next frame), e.g. checking that in-node widgets (gradient bar, curve box) scale with the zoom. Requires the window to have a target Graph Texture (create_graph_texture) for it to render nodes.

zoom.description: View scale (> 0). 1.0 = native, 2.0 = 2x zoom in, 0.5 = 2x zoom out.

name: texture_graph_set_view

description: Set the Geometry Graph window's canvas selection: clears the current canvas selection and selects the given node ids (empty / omitted node_ids just clears) and optionally a link. A selected link shows its pen-tool tangent dots on the canvas and a link section in Node Properties. Also shows the Geometry Graph and Node Properties windows so the selection and its properties are observable in the next capture_screenshot. Nodes must have rendered at least once (show the window first, e.g. geometry_graph_set_view).

link.description: Link to select, identified by its endpoint pins: {source_node_id, source_slot, sink_node_id, sink_slot} (slots default 0)

node_ids.description: Ids of the nodes to select (see get_geometry_graph); empty clears the selection

name: geometry_graph_select_nodes

description: Set the Texture Graph window's canvas node selection: clears the current canvas selection and selects the given node ids (empty / omitted node_ids just clears). Also shows the Texture Graph and Node Properties windows so the selection and its properties are observable in the next capture_screenshot. Nodes must have rendered at least once (show the window first).

node_ids.description: Ids of the nodes to select (see get_texture_graph); empty clears the selection

name: texture_graph_select_nodes

description: Set a geometry graph node's canvas layout: position, requested width / height (canvas units; content is not scaled - the node gets more room; 0 = automatic, content taller/wider than the request wins), and which node edge the input / output pins are laid out on. All arguments except node_id are optional; omitted ones are left unchanged. Returns the resulting layout. Same knobs as the Node Properties window's Position / Size / Inputs / Outputs rows.

height.description: Requested node height in canvas units; 0 = automatic (content-derived)

input_edge.description: Edge for input pins: left (default) or right

node_id.description: Id of the node (see get_geometry_graph)

output_edge.description: Edge for output pins: left or right (default)

pin_label_width.description: Pin label column width in canvas units (default 70; clamped to 20..400)

width.description: Requested node width in canvas units; 0 = automatic (content-derived)

name: geometry_graph_set_node_layout

description: Set a texture graph node's canvas layout: position, requested width / height (canvas units; content is not scaled - the node gets more room; 0 = automatic, content taller/wider than the request wins), and which node edge the input / output pins are laid out on. All arguments except node_id are optional; omitted ones are left unchanged. Returns the resulting layout. Same knobs as the Node Properties window's Position / Size / Inputs / Outputs rows.

height.description: Requested node height in canvas units; 0 = automatic (content-derived)

input_edge.description: Edge for input pins: left (default) or right

node_id.description: Id of the node (see get_texture_graph)

output_edge.description: Edge for output pins: left or right (default)

pin_label_width.description: Pin label column width in canvas units (default 70; clamped to 20..400)

width.description: Requested node width in canvas units; 0 = automatic (content-derived)

name: texture_graph_set_node_layout

description: Create a Graph Texture asset (a procedural texture backed by a node graph) in a scene (under parent_id / parent_name, else in its kind Scope) and point the Texture Graph window at it (its new target). The window's target Graph Texture is what the texture_graph_* tools operate on (retarget later with set_texture_graph_target). A Material slot can then source from it (set_material_texture_source). Returns the new asset's id and name.

name.description: Name of the new Graph Texture asset (must be unique in the scene)

parent_id.description: Id of the prim to create the Graph Texture under (any prim: an Xform, a Mesh, a Scope, another resource, ...). Without parent_id / parent_name the Graph Texture goes into its kind Scope of the scene

parent_name.description: Name (must name exactly one prim) or path ('Parent/Child', or '/Child' for a child of the scene root) of the prim to create the Graph Texture under; alternative to parent_id

name: create_graph_texture

description: Bind a Material texture slot to a Graph Texture asset so the material samples the graph's baked output (the material->graph back-reference; editing the graph updates the material live). Each slot holds a single texture reference, so binding replaces any previously assigned texture. Omit or empty 'graph_texture' to clear the slot entirely.

graph_texture.description: Name of the Graph Texture asset to source from; empty to clear the binding

material_name.description: Name of the material in the scene's content library

slot.description: Texture slot: base_color (default), metallic_roughness, normal, occlusion, or emissive

name: set_material_texture_source

description: List the Graph Texture assets in a scene's content library (or all scenes when scene_name is omitted): name, id, scene, node_count, and has_output (whether the graph currently bakes an output texture).
name: get_graph_textures

description: Create a Graph Mesh asset (a procedural mesh backed by a geometry node graph) in a scene (under parent_id / parent_name, else in its kind Scope) and point the Geometry Graph window at it (its new target). The window's target Graph Mesh is what the geometry_graph_* tools operate on (retarget later with set_geometry_graph_target). A scene Node can then source its mesh from it (set_node_graph_mesh). Returns the new asset's id and name.

name.description: Name of the new Graph Mesh asset (must be unique in the scene)

parent_id.description: Id of the prim to create the Graph Mesh under (any prim: an Xform, a Mesh, a Scope, another resource, ...). Without parent_id / parent_name the Graph Mesh goes into its kind Scope of the scene

parent_name.description: Name (must name exactly one prim) or path ('Parent/Child', or '/Child' for a child of the scene root) of the prim to create the Graph Mesh under; alternative to parent_id

name: create_graph_mesh

description: Bind a scene Node to a Graph Mesh asset by writing the node's Geometry_graph_mesh.graph_mesh value: the node's renderable mesh (and optional physics) is sourced from the graph's baked output, and the value points back at the asset (the node->graph back-reference; editing the graph updates the node's mesh live). Omit or empty 'graph_mesh' to clear the value and release the controlled mesh. Scene state reflects the bake after the next evaluation completes (get_geometry_graph is the barrier). This tool is not undoable; set_item_property on Geometry_graph_mesh.graph_mesh writes the same value through the undo stack.

graph_mesh.description: Name of the Graph Mesh asset to source from; empty to remove the binding

node_name.description: Name of the scene node to bind

name: set_node_graph_mesh

description: List the Graph Mesh assets in a scene's content library (or all scenes when scene_name is omitted): name, id, scene, node_count, baked_revision and has_bake (whether the graph has published baked products).
name: get_graph_meshes

description: List the procedural texture node graph the Texture Graph window currently targets: the target asset name/id, nodes with ids, type labels, canvas positions, parameters, input pins (slot, value type, whether connected, source node id/slot) and output pins (slot, value type), plus a 'composable' flag per node, and all links. 'selected' is true when the window has a target. Texture graph evaluation is synchronous, so no wait is needed.

graph_texture.description: Name of the Graph Texture asset to target; empty or omitted clears the target

name: texture_graph_add_node

sink_node_id.description: Id of the node receiving the input

sink_slot.description: Input pin slot index on the sink node (default 0)

source_node_id.description: Id of the node providing the output

source_slot.description: Output pin slot index on the source node (default 0)

name: texture_graph_disconnect

description: Remove a texture graph node (its links are removed too). Undoable.

node_id.description: Id of the node to remove

name: texture_graph_remove_node

description: Set parameters of a texture graph node. Takes the same JSON object shape as the graph file's per-node 'parameters' (see get_texture_graph); partial updates are allowed - omitted keys keep their current values. Undoable.

node_id.description: Id of the node

name: texture_graph_set_parameter

description: Compose and render a texture graph node's output to a PNG file. For a generator/filter node the given output slot is rendered; for the Output node (no output pins) the connected input's subtree is rendered. Returns the written path and its width/height. Requires the graphics device (works in the headless Vulkan build).

dir.description: Output directory (created if missing); files are named <base_name>_<channel>.png

description: Open a new Geometry Graph window (in addition to the primary one), optionally targeting a named Graph Mesh asset. Multiple windows can target different assets at once (issue #252).

Times/values apply to the channel's sampler, so channels sharing a sampler are affected together.

get_draw_lists
description: Inspect the scene's persistent draw lists (Draw_list_scene, doc/draw_list_renderer_requirements.md): registered object count, draw list / entry counts, pending (unflushed) change count and runtime negative-determinant flip count. verbose=true also lists every non-empty draw list with its identity key. has_draw_lists=false when the scene root has no Draw_list_scene (preview / tool scenes). Also reports resolution diagnostics: color_environment_change_count (each change re-resolves every color list), lazy_resolution_count (one-off first-use resolutions), material_change_count (material identity changes that re-registered objects). Supplying mesh_name or mesh_id adds an entries array for that one mesh: per entry its draw list / entry index, mesh_primitive_index, identity key, the material_index its CACHED primitive record was written with (what the draw actually resolves the material through), and the live Mesh_primitive's material_id / material_name / material_buffer_index. A material_index that disagrees with the material the mesh names is a stale cached record.

Report every cross-frame reference the editor parts cache: the animation window / player target, each Properties window's target and inspected material, the brush tool's active and drag-and-drop brush, the material paint tool, material preview, BRDF slice, Operations make-mesh material, Create brush, physics tool target mesh, each graph editor window target, each item tree's hovered / popup item and cached row count, each grid's frame node, and the selection. description: Inject erhe::window::Input_event values into the editor's window, the way real keyboard, mouse and controller input arrives: the events travel get_input_events() -> Editor::dispatch_input_event -> the ImGui hosts and erhe::commands, so every consumer of real input sees them (ImGui widgets, viewport tools, the fly camera). This is the way to exercise the menu- and mouse-driven entry points headlessly; scene scripting keeps using the explicit-argument tools. Each event carries a 'frame' offset and the call spans that many editor frames, returning one frame after the last event was dispatched - so a capture_screenshot right after it already shows the result. One gesture runs at a time: a second call while one is stepping is an error. In the windowed build injected events interleave with the user's real input. Pointer coordinates are window pixels with the origin at the top left, the space get_viewports reports its rectangles in. See doc/agents/mcp_ui_driving.md.

With hold the button stays down - report it with get_input_state and end the drag with mouse_release. The call spans the frames the gesture needs and returns one frame after the last event was dispatched, so a capture_screenshot right after it already shows the result. description: Report where the transform gizmo's handles are, in the editor window pixels mouse_drag aims at. The gizmo has no meshes - it is hit tested analytically - so this runs the editor's own handle pick over a grid of rays through the gizmo's screen area and returns, per handle currently shown, a point that picks that handle (the sample deepest inside its region) plus the world point the ray hits. Each entry carries the handle's name (which names the axis, not the direction) and handle_value, the Handle enumerator debug_set_transform_hover takes. Also reports the gizmo anchor and its radius. Requires a selection; pass 'viewport' to probe a viewport other than the first. A rotate ring entry also carries ring_axis, the world axis that ring turns about, and euler_gimbal: in Euler gimbal mode (Transform window Rotation shown as Euler Angles, Orthogonal Gizmo off) the rings are the Euler order's rings, so the handle named 'Rotate X' is the first ring of the order (for ZYX it turns about Z) - choose a ring by ring_axis, not by name. Pass probe_points to also get, per given window point, the handle it picks (handle / handle_value, 'None' / 0 for no handle) in 'probes' - to confirm a grab point before a mouse_drag, since a rotate ring is only a few pixels wide where it crosses another.

probe_points.description: Window points [[x, y], ...] to report the picked handle for

viewport.description: Viewport window title (default: the first viewport showing a scene through a camera)

name: get_transform_handles

description: Report what the Transform window's Rotation group shows: its representation (Quaternion / Matrix / Axis-angle / Euler Angles), the Euler order, the three Euler angles in degrees exactly as the row displays them, and the quaternion. The Euler angles need not be a canonical extraction of the node's rotation: several angle triples give the same quaternion, and the row keeps the one nearest to the angles it showed before (what the user dragged or typed). The Transform window must be visible and a node selected for the values to track the selection.

description: Turn the source viewport (the last hovered one, else the only one) into a four view: creates three session-only orthographic cameras (Top, Front, Right) in the viewport's scene, framed on the scene's mesh bounds, opens a viewport window for each, and docks the four windows as a 2 x 2 grid sharing one cross splitter (top | front over right | source). The four cameras share one focus point, the point a fixed distance ahead of the source viewport's perspective camera: moving or turning the perspective camera moves the orthographic cameras, and moving an orthographic camera in its view plane moves the other two and translates the perspective camera by the same offset. The orthographic views also share one zoom, and their rotation is locked. Returns the four view (same shape as one get_four_views entry). See doc/editor/four_view.md.

description: Report where loaded content's memory sits: per-pool mesh vertex/index bytes (capacity only ever grows because pool blocks are never destroyed, so 'used_bytes' is the figure that drops when meshes are released), estimated texture bytes and count, the driver memory budget (Vulkan only), the cached bottom-level acceleration structure count, mesh optimization totals (mesh_optimization: how many primitives were optimized, how many of those replayed from the disk cache, vertex counts and vertex-fetch bytes before and after, and triangle-weighted ACMR and overdraw before and after - session-wide and cumulative, and the right place to read them because geometry-path optimizations land asynchronously after a load), undo/redo entry counts, and the loaded asset containers. Mesh and texture releases are frame-deferred, so advance a few frames before sampling after a removal. See doc/reloadable-asset-loads.md.
name: get_memory_usage

description: Give back the memory of undone glTF loads that the automatic drop declined. Releases the payload of the load that would be redone first, and DISCARDS every redo entry recorded after it - those entries hold references to the released content, so they cannot survive it. Redo entries recorded before the load are untouched. Redoing the released load re-reads the file. Reports released_count and discarded_count. See doc/reloadable-asset-loads.md.
name: free_undone_loads

description: List the registered properties of one item (doc/property-system.md): for each, its name, type (bool, int, float, vec2, vec3, vec4, quat, string, enum, object), effective value, value source (default, inherited, local), local value (null when the item has no local value), default, read_only, inherits, coerced, consequence flags, and enum_labels for enumerations. Values are strings: 'true'/'false', numbers, space-separated vector components, quaternions as 'x y z w', enumeration labels. Also lists attached properties that have a local value on the item. Identify the item by item_id (unique item id, any scene) or item_name - a name or a path (doc/usd-compatibility-plan.md M1) - in scene_name, or the first scene; nodes, node attachments (meshes, lights, cameras, ...) and content-library materials are found, and a grid (owned by the Grid tool, in no scene) is found by its name or id after the scene lookup. The item carries 'sealed' (lock_edit, writes refused) and 'style' (the name of its style layer or null, see set_item_style); a property's 'source' is one of default, inherited, style, local, expression. An 'object' property references another item: its value is the referenced item's reference text (its path when it is in a hierarchy, its name otherwise), with reference_id (session item id), reference_type and reference_item_types (the accepted Item_type mask) alongside; a material's texture slots are object properties. 'sub_objects' lists the item's property sub-objects (a mesh's primitives: index, label and their properties, e.g. a primitive's 'material'); write them with set_item_property's sub_object. Each property of the item itself also carries 'origin' (doc/usd-compatibility-plan.md X5): where the value comes from in the terms of the file the scene was opened from - 'layer' (the file authoring it, 'session' for a scene with no file yet), 'prim_path' (the path in that layer that authors it), 'arc' (none, root layer, reference, payload, inherits), 'arc_target' (the arc's '<file></prim>' target, or the class prim of a style) and 'authored_as' (the attribute a save spells the value as). A sub-object's properties carry no origin.

item_id.description: Unique item id (from get_scene_items / the item tree)

item_name.description: Item name or item path (slash-separated names from the scene root node, or a content-library folder path), looked up in scene_name (or the first scene)

scene_name.description: Scene to look item_name up in (optional)

name: get_item_properties

description: List the attached properties the Properties window's Add Property picker offers for one item (doc/property-system.md R7, D12): every attached registration not already listed for the item, that is, the registering type's visible_when does not hold for it and it holds no local value. Each entry has the fields get_item_properties uses (name is the qualified '<Owner>.<name>', attached true, type, value = the effective value an add would make local, default, label, group, enum_labels). To add one, call set_item_property with that qualified name (any value, or the listed value to change nothing but the layer); to remove it again, set_item_property with a null value. Identify the item by item_id or item_name (in scene_name, or the first scene). include_developer_only lists developer_only registrations too. On a content-library folder the candidates also include the value properties of the folder's category item class by qualified name (a Materials folder: 'Material.base_color', 'Material.roughness', ...; doc/content-library-folders.md D8): a value set on the folder is inherited by every entry below it that has no local value of its own.

item_id.description: Unique item id (from get_scene_items / the item tree)

item_name.description: Item name, looked up in scene_name (or the first scene)

scene_name.description: Scene to look item_name up in (optional)

name: get_addable_item_properties

description: Set one registered property of an item as an undoable operation (Property_set_operation). value is the property's string form (see get_item_properties) - 'true'/'false', a number, space- or comma-separated vector components, a quaternion as 'x y z w', or an enumeration label; a JSON number, bool or array of numbers is accepted too. Pass null (or omit value) to clear the local value so the property falls back to its inherited or default value. Rejected values (wrong type, enumeration label not in the table, failed validate) return an error and change nothing. The write is queued on the operation stack and applied on the next frame. An object property (a material texture slot, a primitive's material) takes value as the referenced item's name (resolved in the item's scene; empty or null clears) or reference_id as its session item id (disambiguates same-named items); the referenced item must belong to the item's scene or be a cross-scene referenceable asset. Pass sub_object to address one of the item's property sub-objects (a mesh primitive index from get_item_properties sub_objects). On a content-library folder, a category property is written by its qualified name ('Material.base_color' on a Materials folder) and cleared with a null value. A grid is addressed by its name or id like any item; its 'frame_node' (the node whose world transform the Node plane follows) takes reference_id, since a grid has no scene to resolve a name in.

item_name.description: Item name, looked up in scene_name (or the first scene)

property.description: Property name as listed by get_item_properties

description: Create an empty style item (doc/style-library.md R1) under a parent prim or in the scene's Styles scope, as one undoable insert executed immediately; returns the style's item id and final (unique) name. A style holds value properties of any class by qualified name ('Light.color', 'Material.roughness'; get_addable_item_properties on the style lists them all): fill it with set_item_property and assign it by setting any item's 'style' property to the style's name. Values of a class the user is not (Light.* on a node) reach the user's inheritance descendants of that class, so a style on an empty node styles the lights below it.

description: Make a style item (doc/style-library.md) in the item's scene Styles folder from the source item's local values, named after the source, and assign it to the item, in one undo entry. The style item is then editable like any item (get_item_properties / set_item_property by qualified name, e.g. 'Material.roughness'), and every item using it follows the edit live. To assign an existing style, set_item_property the item's 'style' property to the style's name (or reference_id); a null value clears it (same as clear_item_style).

description: Set app-wide graphics settings that are not part of a graphics preset. 'headlight_when_unlit' (default true) lights a scene whose light layer is empty with one white directional light along each viewport camera's axis, the way usdview lights a stage that authors no light; false renders such a scene black. 'sky_enabled' and 'grid_visible' (both default true) turn the editor's own sky background and grid off for the rest of this editor run, which is how automated capture flows get an image holding only what the scene file authors; they are session-only and leave the stored settings untouched. Returns the values in effect after the call.
